expectations.text: Starts with an anti-vision: detailed writing of the life you don't want until uncomfortable
Then a vision derived from the anti-vision; big, emotionally compelling; 'dance between' them for daily decisions
Purpose turned into a big goal / path of mastery
Breaks into yearly, monthly, weekly and daily goals
Mentions self-discipline as desire for highest self outweighing cheap pleasures, or goals that repel distractions
Gives concrete prompts/questions to answer
'You are the niche' — most profitable niche is you (overlap of skills, interests, experience) rather than niching down into work you hate
Skill stack / specialized generalism
Message (capture attention; relatable/understandable/actionable) and Medium (distribution equals freedom)
Results-oriented skills: write, speak, market, sell
Project to product: get paid for problems you solve for yourself; take projects public
Start as one person rather than a big company (and/or cites Koe's revenue progression with caveat)
Names the three pillars: focus, energy, experience
Energy: 'energy flows where attention goes'; mental energy = attention, intention, will
Experience: what's in front of you / present moment; enjoyment
Level of mind: every problem demands increasing level of mind (openness of perspective), solved via self-education, self-experimentation, persistence
expectations.evidence: Level of mind defined per book
